minor.issue: Rate-limit row inserted BEFORE the user lookup, so 3 calls on an unknown email still consume the quota for that email. Not a security issue (neutral response stays neutral), but a malicious actor could DOS-block password resets for a specific (known) email. Recommend insert AFTER the user check, or accept current behaviour as anti-enumeration timing equalisation.

No TTL index on db.password_resets.ts (rows accumulate). Same recommendation as iter23 for resend_attempts. Add createIndex('ts', expireAfterSeconds=86400). Also add same on db.password_reset_tokens.expires_at (auto-cleanup expired tokens) — backend cleanup task partially covers this but a Mongo TTL is more robust.

rca of the issue: FIXED BUG: AuthContext.js axios response interceptor checked isAuthEndpoint for /login, /register, /verify-email, /verification-status, /forgot-password, /reset-password, /sms/* — but NOT /auth/me. On /reset-password page mount, AuthContext calls /auth/me to bootstrap user state. For an unauthenticated visitor (the common case for password reset), this returns 401 → interceptor falsely treats it as 'session expired' → redirects to /login?reason=session_expired. User never sees the reset form. Fix: add /api/auth/me to isAuthEndpoint AND add a public-page guard so any 401 occurring on /, /login, /sms-login, /verify-email, /reset-password is silently ignored (no redirect).
